_comment_1: The facts about a package that decide whether a requirement applies to it. A condition code is NOT a legal claim - it is a question the framework needs to be able to ask. What the law does with the answer lives on the requirement, in rules.json, through a REQUIRES / EXEMPTS / SCOPE_GATE link.
_comment_2: 'determination' is the field that matters and it is mostly 'not_determinable'. That is the honest state of this system, not an oversight: rules/INVENTORY.md records that Product carries no net quantity, commodity type, import status, buyer type or package-role as APPLICABILITY INPUTS, and that this is the single widest correctness caveat in the project.
_comment_3: NOTHING HERE MAY BE INFERRED FROM OCR. A package that omits an importer's name is not thereby domestic - it may be unlawful, or badly photographed. INVENTORY.md states the point directly against rule 6(1)(aa): inferring import status from the presence of importer_name would make the rule self-fulfilling, because a package omitting both would look exempt.
_comment_4: Some conditions below carry no requirement link at all. They are the special categories the project must be able to represent (Step 1 brief) for which the verified material in rules/SOURCES.md and rules/INVENTORY.md establishes no clause. Those say so in determination_note and must not be attached to a requirement until a named reviewer supplies the source.

conditions.name: Ordinary packaged commodity intended for retail sale
conditions.description: A pre-packed commodity intended for retail sale, to which Chapter II applies in the ordinary way - i.e. none of the scope gates in rule 3 or rule 26 removes it.
conditions.determination_note: Cannot be established affirmatively, because it is the absence of every scope gate below and those gates are themselves not determinable. Treating a submission as ordinary by default is exactly the over-application rules/INVENTORY.md records against rule 3 and rule 26.

conditions.name: Package containing food articles
conditions.description: A package containing food articles, for which Explanation III to rule 6(1)(a) disapplies that clause in favour of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and the rules made thereunder.
conditions.determination_note: The one condition in this file that IS determinable today: the 'packaged-food' ProductCategory expresses it, and LM-PC-0001 already encodes the carve-out by targeting 'packaged-non-food' only. Note the category is an internal grouping (see seed_categories.py), so it records how a submission was classified, not an adjudication that the contents are food articles within the meaning of the FSS Act.

conditions.name: Imported product or imported package
conditions.description: A product imported into India. Triggers rule 6(1)(aa) (country of origin), the importer limb of rule 6(1)(a) and rule 10(1), and rule 6(10A) for e-commerce listings.
conditions.determination_note: Not recorded anywhere on Product and NOT inferable from extraction. rules/INVENTORY.md: 'Inferring it from the presence of importer_name would make the rule self-fulfilling: a package that omits both would look exempt.' INVENTORY calls rule 6(1)(aa) the closest requirement in the Rules to implementable - it needs this one applicability input, not a new check type. STEP 2: this fact is now COLLECTABLE - a submitter can state it through ProductApplicabilityDeclaration, and the engine reads it before evaluating any clause it gates. It is 'user_declared', not 'verified': the system records who said so and never confirms it against the package. Left unstated it is UNKNOWN, and a clause turning on it reaches REVIEW_REQUIRED rather than a verdict.

conditions.name: Multi-piece package
conditions.description: A package containing more than one individually packaged or labelled piece of the same commodity, intended for retail either individually or as a whole.
conditions.determination_note: RECORDED AS VOCABULARY ONLY. The Step 1 brief requires this special category to be representable. The project's verified material (rules/SOURCES.md, rules/INVENTORY.md) does not transcribe the rule 2 definition or attach a clause to it, so no requirement links to it and the description above must be treated as a working gloss, not as legal text, until a named reviewer supplies the definition from the source.

conditions.name: Group package

conditions.determination_note: RECORDED AS VOCABULARY ONLY - see 'multi-piece-package'. No clause in the verified material is attached to it.

conditions.name: Combination package
conditions.description: A package containing two or more individually packaged commodities of different kinds, sold as a single unit.
conditions.determination_note: RECORDED AS VOCABULARY ONLY - see 'multi-piece-package'. Note that rule 6(1)(b), which IS transcribed, addresses 'packages with more than one product' and rule 6(5) addresses multi-component commodities; whether either is the operative provision for a combination package is a question for a named reviewer, not an inference to be made here.

conditions.determination_note: Needs the Third Schedule as a reference dataset plus a commodity identification. Without it, the rule 11(2)-(3) prohibition on qualifying words cannot be applied safely.

conditions.determination_note: The physical state of the contents is not recorded and is not reliably visible on a label photograph.

conditions.name: Offered for sale through an e-commerce platform

conditions.determination_note: This system analyses photographs of physical packages. An e-commerce obligation attaches to a LISTING, and the listing is not among the inputs. Evaluating rule 6(10) would need the listing page, not the package - a different pipeline, not a different check type. conditions.name: Pan masala
conditions.description: Pan masala.
conditions.determination_note: RECORDED AS VOCABULARY ONLY, because the Step 1 brief names it as a 2026 amendment area. THE PROJECT'S VERIFIED MATERIAL CONTAINS NO PROVISION ABOUT PAN MASALA. Neither G.S.R. 128(E) nor G.S.R. 312(E) - both read in full - mentions it, and the consolidated publication as recorded in rules/SOURCES.md does not either. If such an amendment exists it is very likely in the unretrieved 2022-2025 chain, most plausibly G.S.R. 881(E). A named reviewer must obtain the Gazette text before any requirement is written against this condition. It may also relate to 'tobacco-product' above; that connection is NOT asserted here.

conditions.name: A relaxation has been granted under rule 33
conditions.description: The Central Government may under rule 33 permit a manufacturer or packer to pack for sale by relaxing one or more provisions of the Rules for a reasonable period, with such corrective measures as may be specified.
conditions.determination_note: THE MOST IMPORTANT CONDITION IN THIS FILE for interpreting any output. rules/INVENTORY.md: 'A relaxation granted under rule 33 makes an otherwise-correct finding wrong. The system has no way to know one exists. Every finding it produces is therefore conditional on no relaxation applying.' There is no register of relaxations available to this system. The 2025 amendment further provides that rule 33 relaxations do not apply where the Medical Devices Rules, 2017 apply.

conditions.name: Registration held under Chapter VI
conditions.description: Whether the manufacturer, packer or importer holds the registration rules 27-30 require with the Director or the Controller.
conditions.determination_note: Determinable in principle, but only against a regulator's register that this system does not hold and does not have an interface to. Nothing on a package evidences registration, so this can never be answered from an image - it is 'database' rather than 'not_determinable' to record that the fact does exist somewhere, unlike a buyer's identity.
